When you’re running an ecommerce business,[email marketing](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/email-marketing) isn’t optional. It’s the heartbeat of your customer communication and the foundation of[retention and growth](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/3-profit-protecting-tactics-during-economic-uncertainty) .


But picking the right platform can make or break how effective your email program actually is. Over the years, as founder of[Zettler Digital](https://zettlerdigital.com/?utm_source=klaviyo) , I’ve tested just about everything out there. What separates the good from the great in 2027 isn’t templates or pricing: it’s[data](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/enhance-customer-journey-retention-data) ,[personalization](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/personalization-outperforms-blasts) ,[automation](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/marketing-automation) ,[reporting](https://www.klaviyo.com/features/reporting) , and[deliverability](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/steps-deliverability-spam) .


Here’s how I think about what matters, and which platforms deliver.


## 5 things to look for in an email marketing platform


### 1. Depth and granularity of data


Data is everything. If a platform can’t give you clean, fast, actionable data (that isn’t delayed or watered down) it’s already a non-starter. You need real-time triggers, product-level logic, and the ability to build segments that don’t choke when you add one more filter.Depth and granularity of that data (ideally in all of your owned channels) is what unlocks personalization. Which brings us to our next point.


“Bad data in equals bad data out,” says Ashley Ismailovski, director of email marketing at[SmartSites](https://www.smartsites.com/) . “If you’re working with fragmented data sources, inconsistency with formatting, or poor-quality data, you aren’t putting yourself in a position to succeed.”


> Bad data in equals bad data out.


Ashley Ismailovski director of email marketing, SmartSites


### 2. Personalization that goes deep


Personalization has to go beyond “Hi \[First Name\].” You want behavioral and predictive intelligence baked in. That’s what lets you send the right message automatically, without overcomplicating your set-up or burning hours in spreadsheets.


### 3. Automation beyond batching and blasting


Automation depth matters. Branching, testing, time windows, global throttles—the works. Without that, you’re just batching and blasting. And that’s not a retention strategy.


“The best email marketing platform isn’t the one with the longest feature list,” says Mike Tatum, lifecycle marketing lead at[Prismfly](https://prismfly.com/services/lifecycle-marketing) . “It’s the one that makes it easy to act on customer data and deliver messages that feel timely and relevant.”


> The best email marketing platform is the one that makes it easy to act on customer data and deliver messages that feel timely and relevant.


Mike Tatum CRM and lifecycle leader


### 4. Reporting that shows what’s actually moving the needle


If you can’t see where your revenue is actually coming from (and what’s incremental) you’re not seeing the whole picture. Good reporting shows you which messages move the needle and which ones waste your send volume.


“Attribution models can vary by platform, with some extending the opportunity to brands to change their attribution windows to match their existing reporting settings,” says Ismailovski. “It’s important to find a platform that aligns with the attribution model your brand is already using,” she recommends.


> It's important to find a platform that aligns with the attribution model your brand is already using.


Ashley Ismailovski director of email marketing, SmartSites


### 5. Deliverability that makes all your strategizing worthwhile


No amount of strategy fixes a platform that can’t get emails into inboxes. Strong deliverability infrastructure and compliance tools aren’t nice-to-haves. They’re requirements.


A great email marketing platform will also offer features that help you improve your deliverability over time and keep up with the latest industry requirements.


And if you’re an enterprise brand, add governance, identity, and how well a platform plays with your existing data stack to the list.


## My top 6 email marketing platforms for 2027


### 1. Klaviyo: Best overall for B2C, built to scale for enterprise


If you’re running an ecommerce brand, Klaviyo is the best all-around platform, full stop.


The[data sync with Shopify](https://www.klaviyo.com/ecommerce-integrations/shopify) is instant, segmentation is incredibly fast, and the flow logic is deep enough to run an entire retention engine without any duct tape. I can create triggered flows for[welcome](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/welcome-email-examples) ,[post-purchase](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/post-purchase-emails) ,[replenishment](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/the-email-automation-all-consumable-goods-brands-need-that-many-dont-yet-use) ,[win-back](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/winback-email-campaign-examples) , and everything in between, without needing a developer or third-party add-on. Klaviyo also supports[Shopify Markets](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/45224022467739) with location aware inventory management.


[SMS](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/sms-marketing) and[push notifications](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/mobile-app-marketing) live inside the same ecosystem, so the customer data stays unified across every channel. Reporting is clean, not overcomplicated. And deliverability is consistently excellent.


“For ecommerce brands, the real advantage of Klaviyo is how seamlessly it connects with your store and scales as you grow,” Tatum says.


> For ecommerce brands, the real advantage of Klaviyo is how seamlessly it connects with your store and scales as you grow.


Mike Tatum CRM and lifecycle leader


Where Klaviyo really pulls ahead for bigger brands is the data layer underneath it, the[Klaviyo Data Platform](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/customer-data-platform) (KDP). Every account gets one live profile per customer with no storage caps, and you can connect your store, POS, subscription, and loyalty tools without building pipelines.


If your needs are more complex, Advanced KDP is where it gets interesting. You can store custom data like bookings or subscriptions, clean up messy incoming data, and recognize more returning visitors across browsers and devices. It also lets you connect approved AI tools to your Klaviyo data with proper permissions, which matters when a lot of people (or a global team) touch the account. And if your data team lives in Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, or Redshift, warehouse sync lets those models feed Klaviyo and sends Klaviyo data back out to your BI tools.


Then there’s[Composer](https://www.klaviyo.com/composer) , Klaviyo’s AI marketing agent. The way I think about it is that it changes your job from doing every step to steering. You give it the goal and the context, then review what it comes back with. It can dig through your campaign and flow performance and tell you what to fix next, build campaigns and flows from a brief, and pull in info from the other tools you use. You can have it check in on your account on a schedule, or save your team’s go-to process so you don’t have to re-explain it every time. You still decide what goes live.


Klaviyo also covers customer service now.[Customer Agent](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/customer-agent) , its AI agent, handles the repetitive tasks, like “where’s my order?”, returns, and product recommendations, over email, chat, text, and WhatsApp. When an issue needs a human, it passes the ticket to[Helpdesk](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/helpdesk) with the whole conversation attached, so nobody asks the customer to start over. Because Helpdesk runs on the same customer profile as your marketing, you can even hold promos for anyone with an open ticket. You can also run simulations to test the agent before it ever talks to a real customer.


Best for: ecommerce and B2C brands, from scrappy to enterprise, that want speed, precision, and flexibility in one platform


Downsides: It’s built for B2C, so it’s not the tool for B2B lead nurturing and doesn’t have the core features like lead scoring/routing and activity based sales automation.


Example:[Coffee Beanery](https://www.coffeebeanery.com/) scaled SMS and email under one roof and[grew revenue with faster execution](https://www.klaviyo.com/customers/case-studies/coffee-beanery) .


### 2. Salesforce Marketing Cloud and Braze: Best for enterprise ecosystems and app-first businesses


First, some context: Salesforce agreed in October 2026 to buy Braze. The deal hasn’t closed (Salesforce expects that in its fiscal 2028), and how the two products will fit together, along with roadmap and pricing, is up in the air until the integration is done. If you’re shopping for either one today, factor that in.


It’s important to note that there are two versions of SFMC: Marketing Cloud Engagement, also called ExactTarget, which tends to attract B2C brands, and Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, also called Pardot, which B2B brands use.


[Salesforce Marketing Cloud](https://www.klaviyo.com/compare/klaviyo-vs-salesforce-marketing-cloud) is built for B2B and global companies already running on Salesforce. When it’s configured properly, it’s a machine. It has deep CRM tie-in, heavy segmentation, and serious compliance. But it’s also slow, expensive, and resource-heavy, and the architecture is fragmented, since it’s really a bundle of acquired products stitched together. Salesforce has been moving toward a new version, Marketing Cloud Next, but it’s still a work in progress for plenty of advanced B2C use cases.


Braze works well for mobile-first companies. You get total control over push, in-app, and email, and Canvas is a strong flow builder. But pricing is layered, it’s technical, and it tends to lean on third-party data warehouses, so you’re paying for that tool on top of Braze. You’ll need engineering support to get full value, and for ecommerce it can be overkill if your business doesn’t revolve around an app.


**Best for:** big organizations that live in Salesforce and have Salesforce certified developer resources, or app-first and hybrid (non-commerce) businesses, especially B2B brands.


**Downsides:** high cost, long implementation cycles, complex integrations, and uncertainty about how the combined roadmap and pricing will shake out


### 3. Iterable: Best for multi-brand retailers


[Iterable](https://www.klaviyo.com/sg/compare/klaviyo-vs-iterable) sits in a similar lane as SFMC and Braze. It’s strong for brands managing multiple storefronts or product catalogs under one roof. Marketers can generate, analyze, and optimize campaigns using natural language prompts, which provides transparency and guardrails, along with the ability to audit.


The tradeoff is that data set-up can get messy fast if your structure isn’t clean. You’ll also feel the cost: Iterable is one of the more expensive platforms on the market, and most teams need at least part-time dev support to maintain it.


Best for: multi-brand or omnichannel retailers


Downsides: high cost, steep learning curve, and limited pre-built ecommerce automations


### 4. Listrak: Best for retailers


[Listrak](https://www.klaviyo.com/compare/klaviyo-vs-listrak) has been around forever, and you can tell, in both good and bad ways. For instance, their account teams are deeply involved in helping retail brands run campaigns and automations.


But the integrations aren’t as plug-and-play and flexibility is limited. Their new Listrak Next architecture is more modern but requires replatforming.


Best for: retail brands that want a high-touch service model


Downsides: less flexibility, weaker support, developer dependencies, and slow execution


### 5. HubSpot: Best for sales-driven B2B businesses


If your marketing is tied closely to a sales funnel,[HubSpot](https://www.reddit.com/r/Klaviyo/comments/1grltqf/why_use_klaviyo_over_app_like_hubspot/) is tough to beat. The CRM connection is seamless, and automation between marketing and sales is smooth.


For ecommerce, though, HubSpot is light. Ecommerce brands usually operate using a B2C workflow, which tends not to translate well with B2B platforms.


Best for: B2B with long sales cycles and sales representatives that work in stages


Downsides: limited ecommerce features and shallow product logic


### 6. Mailchimp: Best for small businesses and beginners


[Mailchimp](https://www.klaviyo.com/compare/klaviyo-vs-mailchimp) is where a lot of people start, and for good reason. It’s easy to use, it has[polished templates](https://www.klaviyo.com/features/email-templates) , and it gets you sending quickly.


But you’ll[hit the ceiling](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/5-brands-finding-success-by-canceling-mailchimp) fast. Data management relies on tags, segmentation is basic, and advanced automations are clunky. Mailchimp’s SMS tool is still basic, and its reporting inflates results with overly generous attribution windows.


Best for: small businesses or creators who just need to send newsletters with no segmentation


Downsides: limited data retention, weak ecommerce features, and scalability issues

## Which email marketing platform is best for your brand?


The right email platform should make your marketing faster, smarter, and more connected, not more complicated.


If you’re in ecommerce, Klaviyo is the best all-around choice in 2027. It’s built around real-time data, not delayed reports. It scales from startup to enterprise without breaking, and the data platform underneath it can handle custom data, identity resolution, and your warehouse as you grow. It gives marketers full control without needing engineers to babysit every change.


The other tools on this list have strengths, especially for mobile or enterprise ecosystems. But for ecommerce growth, nothing beats being able to move fast with clean data and deep automation.


In short: choose the platform that gives you speed and visibility. The rest follows.
